inputs.root_cause: SAL-XLIFF-OBL-009F2EB91831B248 (resource-resolution path traversal) and SAL-XLIFF-OBL-130340BC212989D5 (algorithmic-complexity/checked-arithmetic) both XLIFF-SEC-001. The first already carried a precise finding identical in shape to UBL-SEC-001's SAL-UBL-OBL-4CA52BA5DDD8840F (no resolution feature exists, correctly left missing pending a dedicated proof); the second already had depth/node-count limits implemented and tested, but no test covered a width-shaped complexity vector distinct from depth.
inputs.acceptance_evidence: 6 new tests prove the same absence-of-attack-surface pattern already used for UBL-SEC-001 (AST scan plus a monkeypatched-filesystem behavioral proof across 4 hostile path shapes stored in a <note> element). 2 new tests prove _enforce_tree_limits bounds a wide-but-shallow (quadratic-blowup-style) document by node count, a distinct vector from the already-tested deep-nesting case.
inputs.regression_tier: full xliff package suite (tests/python/xliff) plus 6-format regression

execution_steps: 1. Re-confirmed the obligation's own prior finding was not stale: grepped the whole xliff package for open(/Path(/.read_bytes()/os.path -- the only 2 hits are reader.py's caller-supplied top-level source path and writer.py's caller-supplied destination path, neither derived from parsed document content. Checked model/document.py: no href/OriginalData/typed reference-bearing dataclass exists anywhere; the only free-text carrier is Note.text, a plain string field.

2. Ran an interactive probe before writing any test: built a document with a hostile path-traversal string inside a <note> element, monkeypatched Path.open/Path.read_bytes to raise if ever called, then ran loads()/validate()/dumps()/loads() against it across 4 hostile URI shapes -- confirmed zero filesystem access, on the first attempt, mirroring the UBL-SEC-001 pattern exactly.
3. Wrote 6 tests in a new file: the AST-scan (forbidden-module import check) and a parametrized 4-shape behavioral proof using pytest's monkeypatch fixture.

4. For the second obligation, read _enforce_tree_limits (reader.py) directly: it walks the tree with an explicit stack, checking both max_xml_nodes and max_nesting_depth on every node visited -- confirming node-count bounding is already real and would catch a wide-but-shallow document even though only the deep-nesting case had a dedicated test. Verified interactively with a 10000-sibling, depth-3 document against a tight max_xml_nodes limit -- correctly refused on the first attempt.
5. Added 2 tests to the existing test_obligation_security_limits.py file, extending its established fixture-building pattern (_nested -> _wide).

6. Ran ruff (clean) and the full xliff suite (358 passed, was 350, +8) before writing any evidence claim. Ran the full 6-format regression (3096 passed, was 3088, +8; same 4 pre-existing unrelated safetensors interop failures, 2 skipped) confirming zero cross-format regression.
tests_run: .venv/Scripts/pytest tests/python/ipynb tests/python/ora tests/python/nrrd tests/python/xliff tests/python/safetensors tests/python/ubl -q -- 3096 passed, 2 skipped, 4 preexisting unrelated safetensors interop failures, was 3088 passed

evidence.oracle: SELF-CONSISTENT format_factory-only evidence per the execution-recovery directive's GAP-008 rule, not cross-checked against a reference XLIFF implementation.
evidence.obligations_moved_breakdown: 1 obligation (SAL-XLIFF-OBL-009F2EB91831B248) promoted from missing to implemented by proving the required safety property directly. The second obligation (SAL-XLIFF-OBL-130340BC212989D5) gains a genuine new complexity-vector test but stays honestly partial -- its own missing_behavior text also asks for a distinct 'checked arithmetic' guarantee test, which was judged the same way this session characterized the equivalent UBL/NRRD obligations: Python's native big-int semantics make a dedicated checked-arithmetic test largely redundant with the count/depth-limit tests already present, not a separate exploitable gap, but the citation was left narrowed rather than force-closed.
